doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23

title: Playing funerals and for the Davy Crockett and Owls
summary: Laine says his band played funerals, dances and parades for benevolent associations and the Owls; La Rocca could not play a funeral.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Well, I wanted to ask something about those funerals. You said Nick La Rocca didn't play any funerals, but did your band play for some of the funerals?
He didn't know no more about playing the funeral than you.
No, but did you play the funeral?
Oh, did I? Sure did. Sure, there's his...

I belonged to David. I played for them. I used to play all their dances, all their balls, all their parades. You leave Benevolent Association, I played all their parades and all their dances and all their... All their barrails, all their funerals.
Anyway. Did you play very many funerals? How often did they have a funeral that way with music? Oh, not very often, no.
No, I don't think they did. No. I don't think they did, really. I don't believe it. No. I don't believe it.
You know, when they used to play... When did they stop playing funerals with music? I mean, was this back in the 90s or was this back...
When did they start playing music for funerals? In what year? You don't remember?

I really don't. And I ain't gonna say I do because I don't. I don't know. Oh, I know he don't. He don't remember. I don't... I never paid that much mind outside of the records. I used to... I used to keep those records and the contracts. From whom, where, when and what. Keep them all in together. I had a trunk load of that stuff, I tell you.
